title: Seeing Him everywhere
hookLine: with cleared eyes, He is seen within and without (Sukhmani 23)
last: GIAAN ANJAN — THE GURU CLEARED MY EYES.

lines: LOOKING FOR THE GLASSES YOU'RE WEARING.
cards: You can lose your glasses while wearing them. Patting every pocket, checking under the couch cushions, asking the whole house, until someone points at your face.
The thing you were searching for was right there, closer than anything else, which is exactly why you couldn't find it.
Gurbani makes a similar point, in earnest: the One we go searching for is seen, by cleared eyes, both within and without.

teach.b: The first stanza after the salok begins, in paraphrase: in the company of the holy, I saw God within. God's Name began to taste sweet. All things are held within the One, appearing in many colors.
Antar is within, the inner self. The cleared eyes look in first and find God there: antar prabh deethaa, God seen inside. But the stanza doesn't stop at the inner room.
It turns outward, to all things and their many colors, all held in the One. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, puts the two directions side by side in a hymn in raag Dhanasari.
In paraphrase: why go searching in the forest? God lives in everything, yet stays untouched, and is with you too.

teach.h: FRAGRANCE IN A FLOWER, A FACE IN A MIRROR.
teach.b: Like fragrance in a flower, like a reflection in a mirror, God dwells within; search in your own heart. Within and without, know the One. That, he says, is the wisdom the Guru gave.
Two pictures. You can't see the fragrance in the flower, but it's all through it. You can't pull the reflection out of the mirror, but it's really there.
That's how the Gurus speak about God within.
The hymn speaks to seekers who leave home for the forest to find God, and its answer is gentle: you don't have to go anywhere. Look in, then look around. The same One is in both places.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-third ashtpadi hear that God is seen within, in the company of the holy, and then in all things; Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymn teaches knowing the One within and without.

o: a time of waiting between two lives
within, the inner self where God is seen
a deep forest where seekers go to pray

games.q: seeing Him everywhere — tap the pairs.
p: where you don't need to go

s: the stanza finds God only inside, never in the world
it looks within first, then outward to all things in many colors.
Guru Tegh Bahadur asks why anyone should search in the forest
God lives in everything, and within your own heart.
in the hymn, God is pictured like a reflection in a mirror
and like fragrance in a flower: really there, though you can't pull it out.

games.q: you want to find God, and a friend suggests leaving everything for a forest retreat. what does Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymn ask?
o: why go searching in the forest? look in your own heart.
games.why: why go to the forest? God dwells within, like fragrance in a flower. within and without, know the One.

practice: For the first minute, close your eyes and rest inside, the breath, the heartbeat, the quiet under the thoughts, hunting for nothing.
Then open your eyes slowly and look around the room or out the window with the same quiet attention, letting inside and outside sit together. If you pray, say Waheguru once inward, once outward.

wordCard.voice: Antar, within, inside: cleared eyes find God antar, and then in all things outside; Guru Tegh Bahadur says: within and without, know the One.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: antar, within, inside; antar prabh deethaa, God seen within.

carryVoice: Your line: within and without. No forest required, only cleared eyes. That's day five hundred twenty-seven.

sources.ref: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 23, pauri 1 (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 293)
Raag Dhanasari, Guru Tegh Bahadur (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 684)
